decisions.reason: F9 attributed analytic holomorphy to a pointwise definition. The existing slit-plane corollary supplies Log and its rotated branches; product/reciprocal rules supply integer powers. The meridian integral is -2πm, conjugate periods vanish on the simply connected surface, and removable singularities give exactly the asserted divisor. Corrected F3 to cite the Cauchy–Riemann equivalence. Statement and page interface unchanged.

F11 cited a pointwise definition for holomorphic sector powers. The barrier is now explicitly exp(mu Log(-iw)); the rotated sector has argument strictly between -pi and pi, so the published slit-plane corollary, entire exponential and chain rule license holomorphy. Smoothness and the C2 component theorem give harmonicity, and the narrower interior sector supplies the positive cosine bound. The regular-level exhaustion, Perron modification/Harnack limit and two boundary barriers retain both contract claims and Countable Choice. Removed an unnecessary pre-connectedness assertion about the interior closure. Statement unchanged.

F8 and step 14.1 called a circle mean A_w although the cited corollary requires ball means. The repair integrates the already proved circle identity over concentric radii, producing the disc identity exactly, and invokes the published plane converse whose definition includes both means. Poisson radial estimates, finite oscillation covers, deterministic diagonal selection and uniform Cauchy convergence preserve the subsequential claim. Distributional convergence commutes with Delta on tests and Weyl supplies its unique harmonic representative under Countable Choice. Corrected the compact-closed citation and C^k typo. Statement unchanged.

The zero-based maximizing sequence used an empty maximum at n=0. Starting the finite maximum at v_0 repairs that convention defect without changing any estimate or claim; u_n increases, stays in the Perron family and converges to the supremum at x_0. Harnack applied to Poisson modifications yields the local finite/infinite alternatives; comparison with an arbitrary candidate identifies the finite harmonic limit, connectedness gives the global dichotomy, and logarithmic sandwich/removability and compact-support maximum comparison give the pole and leastness. Locality is now applied on an open exterior. Statement unchanged.

The original preimage containment did not require the closed Euclidean ball to lie in the chart image: X=C, the identity chart on Re(z)>0, a=-2 and rho=1 give an empty removed set. On C the candidates max(0,log(R/|z|)) have compact support and at most a unit pole, and diverge at every nonzero point as R grows. Added the intended closed-ball containment, which the original proof already required, preserving the closed-disc contract. Corrected the topological compactness citation and completed the clopen separation and upper-semicontinuous maximum arguments. The fixed Dirichlet barrier gives delta>0 independent of candidates, so inequalities (5),(6) bound the envelope and dichotomy gives finiteness. Only direct consumer is the assigned dipole lemma; its chosen discs meet the added hypothesis, but its F3 must state it.

F12 used a compact-image theorem restricted to metric spaces; the existing theorem for topological spaces now licenses the ambient-surface applications. Qualified the internal closed disc by chart containment and completed the closed-side argument. Read the complete relevant boundary argument in Gilbarg–Trudinger Lemma 6.18 and Theorem 6.19: continuity, interior C2 harmonicity, smooth arcs and zero data give C2 regularity up to smaller arcs. The explicit extension matches derivatives through order two; finitely many supported manifold bumps patch the extensions on a neighbourhood of the punctured compact closure, so the actual Green-identity prerequisites hold. The two pole boundary terms have opposite signs, and increasing exhaustion gives symmetry. Statement unchanged.

F3 omitted closed-ball containment in a larger chart, making its universal assertion false for a relatively compact slit-annulus chart with annular closure and disconnected exterior. The chosen discs in step 1.1 already have extending coordinates, so F3 and the internal disc-complement lemmas now preserve that exact supplier hypothesis; the Statement is unchanged. Corrected the topological compact-image citation and closed-side argument. Harnack comparisons now explicitly use fixed exterior surfaces, yielding constants independent of t. Replaced the unsupported circle-log formula by harmonic-majorant comparison at the logarithmic puncture. Setting t_n=1/(n+2) keeps every zero-based term strictly between zero and one. Symmetry cancels the reference values; uniform exterior and pole-renormalized bounds pass to the harmonic limit and remove p_0.

The compact superlevel family had M-1/n at the zero index; using M-1/(n+1) defines every term and retains decreasing nonempty closed sets with intersection at the supremum. This is a finite-prefix notation defect, not a failure of the maximum argument. Also made C positive in step 8.1 so its strict contradiction is valid. The exponential of the unit-pole kernel gives a disc-valued holomorphic map with one simple zero; the compact-support maximum bound makes all other kernels finite, symmetry forces the normalized harmonic difference to vanish, and other fibre points would force a logarithmic divergence. Injectivity gives biholomorphy onto a proper simply connected plane domain; the Riemann mapping theorem applies under the declared Axiom of Choice. Statement unchanged.

Step 7.1 originally transported the atlas from an already holomorphic covering, so it could not license the arbitrary quotient N/H used for uniqueness. Added a general quotient construction: finite compact-return sets separate distinct orbits, openness of q carries a countable base to the quotient, and disjoint local sheets provide charts. On each overlap the inverse sections differ locally by one group element, so holomorphic group actions give holomorphic transitions and q is a local biholomorphism. The induced quotient-to-X homeomorphism is then locally holomorphic with holomorphic inverse. For every competing model the same construction makes its projection to X holomorphic; uniqueness of topological universal covers therefore lifts to a biholomorphism, and model inequivalence gives uniqueness. Adopted the normative phase numbering and rechecked all remapped references. The Axiom of Choice remains exactly as declared. Statement unchanged.

statement_comparisons.before:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a connected Riemann surface
([[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]]), let $\varphi:W\to\mathbb C$ be
a chart of $X$, let $a\in\mathbb C$ and $\rho>0$, and put
$$U:=\varphi^{-1}\bigl(B(a,\rho)\bigr),\qquad \overline U=\varphi^{-1}\bigl(\overline B(a,\rho)\bigr),$$
assuming that $\overline U\subseteq W$; thus $\overline U$ is a closed coordinate
disc, compact in $X$. Suppose $X\setminus\overline U\ne\varnothing$ and put
$$Y:=X\setminus\overline U .$$
Then $Y$ is connected, hence a Riemann surface in the complex structure
induced by the charts of $X$, and for every $p\in Y$ the canonical Perron
envelope $g_Y(\cdot,p)$ of [[def-canonical-green-kernel-riemann-surface]] is
finite on $Y\setminus\{p\}$. Equivalently: the exterior $Y=X\setminus\overline U$
admits a finite canonical Green kernel at every pole $p\in Y$.
statement_comparisons.after:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a connected Riemann surface
([[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]]), let $\varphi:W\to\mathbb C$ be
a chart of $X$, let $a\in\mathbb C$ and $\rho>0$ satisfy
$\overline B(a,\rho)\subseteq\varphi(W)$, and put
$$U:=\varphi^{-1}\bigl(B(a,\rho)\bigr),\qquad \overline U=\varphi^{-1}\bigl(\overline B(a,\rho)\bigr),$$
so that $\overline U\subseteq W$ is the closure in $X$ of $U$, a closed
coordinate disc compact in $X$. Suppose $X\setminus\overline U\ne\varnothing$ and put
$$Y:=X\setminus\overline U .$$
Then $Y$ is connected, hence a Riemann surface in the complex structure
induced by the charts of $X$, and for every $p\in Y$ the canonical Perron
envelope $g_Y(\cdot,p)$ of [[def-canonical-green-kernel-riemann-surface]] is
finite on $Y\setminus\{p\}$. Equivalently: the exterior $Y=X\setminus\overline U$
admits a finite canonical Green kernel at every pole $p\in Y$.
